subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw make memory_search chunking respect Markdown headings by default, add an opt-in chunking strategy/config, or defer chunking until the broader Memory MVP/entity design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing chunk boundaries affects retrieval behavior and persisted index identity, and the issue also bundles larger entity/concept/synthesis work that needs product ownership.

options.title: Approve a narrow chunking design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware Markdown chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

options.title: Make heading-aware default
options.body: Adopt heading boundaries as canonical Markdown memory behavior, accepting that existing headed files will reindex and retrieve differently.

options.title: Defer to Memory MVP
options.body: Wait for the memory write/entity pipeline decisions so chunking, extraction, and wiki synthesis land as one coordinated design.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow chunking design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware Markdown chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The immediate unresolved choice is the memory-core API/default and persisted index identity contract, which aligns with Peter Steinberger's feature-history ownership in this area.
